study.title: Automatic Identification of Bioprostheses on X-ray Angiographic Sequences of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Procedures Using Deep Learning

imaging.modality_detail: Conventional fluoroscopy and cine X-ray angiography at 15 and 25 fps during TAVI
imaging.territory_detail: Aortic valve / aortic root during transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI)

data_released.detail: Not publicly available due to privacy restrictions; available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request

annotation.annotator_expertise: Experienced hemodynamic cardiologists (clinical members of the research team), using GIMP

task.task_description: Pixel-wise segmentation of the transcatheter heart valve (THV, Allegra bioprosthesis) on X-ray angiographic frames of TAVI procedures with a U-Net, including hyperparameter tuning (training set size, data augmentation, cross-entropy vs focal loss) and evaluation with new distance/noise metrics D1 and D2 and two binarization schemes (Otsu, PKFP).
task.clinical_application: Automatic THV identification to support TAVI, e.g. assessing device positioning and expansion and extracting quantitative implant parameters

temporal_evidence.quote: The expected inputs are 512 × 512, 8-bit (integer values from 0 to 255), grayscale images and their corresponding labels as binary masks for the training.

method.class_imbalance_handling: Focal loss (alpha=0.25, gamma=2) evaluated during hyperparameter tuning (cross-entropy selected); imbalance-specific metrics D1/D2 and prior-knowledge (PKFP) binarization

G9.quote: THV identification is a class imbalance problem. Therefore, conventional classification metrics used in supervised learning, based on the number of true/false positives and negatives, are not fully suitable on this problem

G11.quote: the possibility of extracting additional value from images gathered during and after the procedure for its evaluation and the prediction of long-term outcomes is still an open challenge

other_limitations: Model not trained on THV shapes during deployment; poor, incomplete segmentation in deployment frames
PKFP binarization requires a priori THV knowledge and is invalid when no device is present
Dice coefficient performs poorly for thread-like THV structure
Fixed 0.5 threshold binarization did not perform correctly
future_work: Extraction of quantitative features from THV segmentations
Real-time checking of device placement and expansion during TAVI
Identification of other THV models and devices from other manufacturers
Identification of ridge structures in X-ray sequences in general
